public_source.note: The public repository exposes the Django application, public_website, surveys, tests, Docker configuration, and local/Docker installation and test instructions.

eligible_license.note: GitHub displays an MIT license label, but the linked LICENSE.md page did not expose its grant text on inspection. The metadata label is not enough to verify the actual covered source and scope.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes automation/configuration source and documents downloadable .penpot files; the release page provides versioned design assets without credentials.

eligible_license.note: GitHub labels the repository MIT and lists a LICENSE file, but the license body and its scope over converted/copied Figma-derived .penpot assets and embedded design materials were not verified.

primary_evidence.note: The repository has a v1.14 asset release and import/use instructions, but the README calls it experimental and states synchronization is disabled for lack of a sponsor; evidence does not resolve whether this is a maintained, agency-published software product rather than a design-asset port.

product_identity: Penpot-importable DSFR design-system asset libraries plus automation/configuration intended to synchronize Figma and Penpot files
agency: Unresolved; repository is under betagouv, but README says the initiative has no sponsor
